prov.aeroclub.desc.t: People who fly for no reason at all, and keep score.

prov.home.desc.t: Your own strip in the middle of the island, and everything it could become.

prov.community.desc.t: They came for the quiet and they mean to keep it. Supplies are welcome. Visitors are a committee matter.

ms.field.round.brief.t: Two sacks, two strips: the Cannery and the Fishing Village, in the order you like. It comes round again.

ms.field.hike.brief.t: Sixty kilos of supplies for the trail crew at the Hiking Strip. The strip is dirt. After rain it is something else.

ms.field.ridge.brief.t: One passenger from the Fishing Village to the Mountainside Strip. You land uphill. You will see why.

ms.field.cannery.brief.t: Eighty kilos out of the Cannery Runway and back to the field. Short strip, full load: mind the far end.

ms.hangar.01.brief.t: Sixty kilos of shoring props from the Fishing Village. The Trust wants the old wartime hangar standing before it wants it pretty.

ms.hangar.02.brief.t: A structural engineer is waiting at the Cannery Runway with a hard hat and an opinion. Bring both.

ms.hangar.03.brief.t: Ninety kilos of roofing sheet from the Fishing Village: all a small aeroplane will take in one go.

ms.hangar.04.brief.t: Eighty kilos of fasteners out of the Cannery Runway. Leonard counted them. Twice.

ms.hangar.05.brief.t: A hundred and twenty kilos in one piece: the motor for the big doors. Not a job for the smallest aeroplane you own.

ms.hangar.05.done.t: She opens. First time since the war. The machines inside are yours to use: I would not know which end to hold.

ms.heritage.01.brief.t: One appraiser to East Point Clearing: a hundred and fifty metres in the trees, the sea at one end. The experts swear it can be done. The experts are not flying.

ms.heritage.02.brief.t: Three metres of carved cedar, three hundred kilos, from the Fishing Village to East Point. It does not come apart. Neither should you.

ms.heritage.02.done.t: It stands. The whole island will come and look at it, and nobody will ask how it got there. You and I will know.

ms.mine.03.brief.t: Sixty kilos from the field, sixty from the Fishing Village, both to Copperhead Mine Street. One big aeroplane or two small trips: the old street does not care.

ms.mine.04.brief.t: The first two paying visitors to the old mine. You land in the middle of the village, as people always did. Try to look as if it is normal.

ms.mine.04.done.t: They loved it. One of them asked if the landing is always like that. I said yes.

ms.mine.tour.brief.t: Two visitors out to Copperhead Mine Street, two back. The regulars of the season.

ms.lumber.01.brief.t: One foreman from Greywater Dock to Cedar Harbour, with a chainsaw he will not check in. Floats only.

ms.lumber.02.brief.t: A hundred and fifty kilos of saws, chain and fuel to Cedar Harbour.

ms.lumber.03.brief.t: Two loggers back to Greywater Dock after three weeks in the trees. Open a window.

ms.lumber.04.brief.t: Two hundred and fifty kilos: the head of the camp's mill, to Cedar Harbour. About all a floatplane with four seats will lift.

ms.lumber.04.done.t: She is cutting. You hear that? That is money.

ms.lumber.run.brief.t: A logger and eighty kilos of supplies to Cedar Harbour. The camp eats, the camp runs.

ms.resort.guests.brief.t: One guest up to Skyline, one back down. Martha's season, a seat at a time.

ms.skyline.03.brief.t: Ninety kilos of kitchen for the lodge at Skyline. The stove is in three pieces. One of them is the heavy one.

ms.obs.01.brief.t: Two passes for the survey: over the summit of Mount Ardent, and over the Mountainside Strip on the way. Pick a day you can see the mountain.

ms.obs.02.brief.t: One scientist and two hundred kilos of instruments, onto the snow at Ardent Altiport. Skis. Uphill. No second try.

ms.obs.03.brief.t: The feasibility round is over and the scientist would like a bath. One passenger from Ardent Altiport to the field.

ms.obs.04.brief.t: Two riggers to Ardent Altiport. The cableway takes steel. It does not take people.

ms.obs.05.brief.t: A hundred and twenty kilos of instruments from the Fishing Village to Ardent: too fragile for the cableway, they say. So they asked a pilot.

ms.obs.06.brief.t: A hundred and fifty kilos for the observatory's second building.

ms.obs.07.brief.t: Two glaziers to Ardent Altiport, and their lunch.

ms.obs.08.brief.t: Two hundred kilos, one crate, do not tilt. To Ardent Altiport.

ms.obs.09.brief.t: Two hundred and fifty kilos of snow groomer for a wider, kinder strip on Ardent. The last time you land on the narrow one.

ms.obs.09.done.t: A station on the highest point of the island, and half of it came up in your aeroplane. The lab is open to you: use it.

ms.booze.01.brief.t: Sixty kilos of "preserves" from the Cannery Runway to the Hiking Strip, after dusk. The label says jam. Nobody is going to read the label.

ms.booze.02.title.t: The same favour, the other way

ms.booze.02.brief.t: Eighty kilos out of the Old Community Runway to the Cannery, before dawn. It turns out the quiet people up there make something worth the trip.

ms.home.01.brief.t: Eighty kilos from the field to your own strip: drain pipe and a hand roller. The Cabin Strip is bumpy, narrow and sometimes mud. It is also the only way in.

ms.home.02.brief.t: Sixty kilos from the Fishing Village: enough to mark a strip and clear a corner to park on.

ms.home.03.brief.t: Two hundred and fifty kilos of timber frame from the Fishing Village. The hunter's shed was fine for one. It is not going to be one.

ms.home.04.brief.t: Two hundred kilos from the field: glass, a stove, a door that shuts.

ms.home.05.brief.t: One passenger, thirty kilos of what she could not leave behind, from the field to the Cabin Strip. Land it gently.

ms.home.05.done.t: It has a door. And a view. You told me it was a shed.

ms.home.06.brief.t: Four hundred and fifty kilos in one crate: a digger small enough to fly and big enough to cut a road to the lake. You do not own an aeroplane that carries it. Yet.

ms.home.07.brief.t: A hundred and twenty kilos of fuel from the Fishing Village. The digger drinks.

ms.home.08.brief.t: A hundred and fifty kilos of dock floats from Greywater to your lake. First landing on Cabin Lake: floats under the aeroplane too.

ms.home.09.brief.t: A hundred kilos of decking from Cedar Harbour to Cabin Lake.

ms.home.10.brief.t: Two hundred and fifty kilos of dock from Greywater. Room for more than one aeroplane, for a reason.

ms.home.11.brief.t: Two hundred kilos of cabin from Cedar Harbour: beds for people who fly in.

ms.home.12.brief.t: Two friends from Greywater to your lake, for the night. They would have brought their own aeroplane. They said yours is nicer.

ms.home.12.done.t: Everybody stayed. Nobody wanted to be the first to leave.

ms.home.13.brief.t: Two hundred and eighty kilos of roof truss from the field: your hangar is about to stop being a shed.

ms.home.14.brief.t: Two hundred kilos of door from the Fishing Village: wide enough for the aeroplanes you have been borrowing space for.

ms.home.14.done.t: Now build something that needs it.

ms.community.01.brief.t: One expert to the Old Community Runway: a path that happens to be straight, and happens to be mud. A small rough aeroplane. The community will meet you at the edge of it. Only at the edge.

ms.community.02.brief.t: Eighty kilos of parts from the Fishing Village to the new strip. Their rock grinder came by sea and has not ground a rock since.

ms.community.03.brief.t: Sixty kilos more for the grinder, from the field. The new strip is two hundred metres of the same mud as the old one.

ms.community.04.brief.t: Ninety kilos of grader blade from the field. Four hundred metres now, and every one of them has a bump.

ms.community.05.brief.t: Eighty kilos of culvert pipe from the Cannery Runway.

ms.community.06.brief.t: Sixty kilos of old mine rail from Copperhead Mine Street: the community has plans for it. The community always has plans.

ms.community.07.brief.t: Ninety kilos of the cloth that keeps gravel on top of a swamp, from the Fishing Village.

ms.community.08.brief.t: Four experts from the field to a kilometre of new gravel. One flight, the committee insists: four arrivals would be four too many. You need a bigger aeroplane.

ms.community.09.brief.t: Three hundred kilos of tower from the field.

ms.community.10.brief.t: Four hundred kilos of hangar frame from the field.

ms.community.11.brief.t: Three hundred and fifty kilos from the Fishing Village: the smallest terminal on any map. It has a bench.

ms.community.11.done.t: The committee has voted. You may land here whenever you bring something. That is the warmest thing we have ever said to anyone.

ms.club.stol.brief.t: The rough strip beside runway 02/20, landing 204 degrees. Touch down past the line and stop. The metres from the line to where you stand are your score. Short of the line is a foul.

ms.club.spot.brief.t: Runway 02/20, landing 204 degrees: one painted line, three hundred metres in. Your first touch, measured from it. Before or after counts the same.

ms.club.pylons.brief.t: Four gates round the field, anticlockwise, under a hundred and fifty metres. The clock runs from the first to the last. Touch a pylon and it costs you three seconds.

ms.club.regular.brief.t: Two gates, four kilometres apart. Cross the second one two minutes after the first: not sooner, not later. The fastest aeroplane wins nothing.

ms.club.tour.brief.t: Three timed legs and three landings: the Fishing Village, the Cannery, home. The three times are added. The landings are not timed: take them as they come.

ms.club.tour.done.t: The club would like your aeroplane in a hangar with a rope in front of it. You may still fly it.

ms.club.breakfast.brief.t: One club member from the field to Skyline, wheels stopped within fourteen minutes of the brakes coming off. The pancakes are served at the top. They are served hot or not at all.

ms.club.breakfast.done.t: Everybody who flew in signed the wall. There is a wall now. There is a house round it.
